verdict.rationale: Plausible's own self-hostable Community Edition lets users run it on infrastructure they choose, which effectively decides where analytics data is stored, and community users confirm running it self-hosted. The evidence never documents a region or residency choice in the hosted cloud service, and self-hosting adds operational burden. Missing for 10: documented region/residency selection for the hosted service, explicit statements on where hosted data is stored, any data-residency guarantees.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: A getting started guide to self-hosting Plausible Community Edition
One huge selling point of using Plausible is that you can self-host it and it's FOSS.
I'm a very happy self-hosted Plausible user for years now.
